packets.title: org-core: refuse to start when ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED is on and the SIEM seal key is missing or invalid
packets.brief: Defect: with ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED=1 (or true) and ORG_CORE_SIEM_SEAL_KEY missing or invalid, org-core boots anyway. internal/http/server.go:74-86 only log.Printf's the NewSIEMSealerFromEnv error, so the SIEM routes stay mounted and answer 503 forever. The fix is boot validation. (1) In internal/http/siem_handlers.go, add an exported func ValidateSIEMDestinationsConfig(getenv func(string) string) error. When siemDestinationsEnabled(getenv) is false it returns nil and reads nothing else. When the flag is on it returns the error from orgcore.NewSIEMSealerFromEnv(getenv), wrapped with the flag name and never including the key value. (2) In cmd/server/main.go, call it right after the existing ValidateRequiredServiceCredentialRegistry check at the top of main(), using os.Getenv, and log.Fatalf("[org-core startup] SIEM destinations validation failed: %v", err) on error, the same way the credential-registry check fails. Keep NewServer's runtime fallback (log plus 503) untouched as defence in depth. Regression tests go in internal/http/siem_handlers_test.go and need a fake getenv: flag off with no key returns nil; flag "1" with no key returns an error; flag on with a malformed key (wrong length or non-base64) returns an error; flag on with a valid 32-byte base64 key returns nil; the error text never contains the key material. Must NOT change: the switch stays default off, and with it off the boot behaviour is identical (no new env read is required). Never log or print the seal key. The files are CRLF, so keep their line endings. Don't touch docker-compose.yml or the scripts.

packets.title: audit-verify CLI: verify the manifest signature and support a sub-range export
packets.brief: Defect: cmd/audit-verify/main.go only reads org_id, last_seq, last_row_hash, checkpoint, attestation and legacy_unchained_rows from the manifest (struct at main.go:97-104). It never checks the manifest signature that the server now produces. That signature is internal/store/compliance.go ComplianceManifest plus ManifestPayload at :254-277, signed via chain.KeyRing.SignPayload at internal/chain/sign.go:209, verifiable with KeyRing.VerifyPayload at sign.go:214. The CLI also always treats manifest last_seq as the chain head (main.go:192-194), so a sub-range export (the manifest's last_seq < head_seq, which the API produces for since/until) is reported broken or truncated_below_attestation even when the rows are intact. The fix: (1) Extend the CLI manifest struct with generated_at, first_seq, count, first_prev_hash, head_seq, head_hash, key_id and signature. Unknown fields are already allowed. (2) When key_id and signature are present, rebuild the payload with store.ManifestPayload (import internal/store and do not duplicate the byte format) and verify it with ring.VerifyPayload. On an invalid signature, exit 2 (broken) with a clear stderr line. On an unknown key id, exit 3 (unverifiable). With no signature, print "manifest: unsigned" in the report and keep today's exit behaviour for full-range exports. (3) Range mode applies when the manifest has head_seq > last_seq. Require a valid manifest signature, otherwise exit 3. Verify the rows from first_seq with FromSeq=first_seq and FromHash=first_prev_hash. Use Head={last_seq,last_row_hash} as the range end. Don't pass a newest attestation above last_seq: it would falsely report truncation. Check that the row count equals manifest count. Print that the range is anchored by the signed manifest rather than by an attestation. Never print a bare "verified" for a range that no signature anchors. Must NOT change: full-range verification results and exit codes for existing inputs (the current main_test.go cases must pass unchanged), the export row format, and anything under internal/store or internal/verifier. The files may be CRLF, so keep their line endings. Add table tests to cmd/audit-verify/main_test.go: signed full manifest verifies; tampered manifest field (for example last_seq or legacy count) gives exit 2; unknown key id gives exit 3; signed sub-range verifies (exit 0) where the old code reported broken; unsigned sub-range gives exit 3; existing unsigned full manifest is unchanged.

packets.title: audit-core: count blocked chain purges and alert on them
packets.brief: Defect: a blocked chained purge only writes an audit_chain_incidents row and a log line (internal/store/attest.go blockPurge at :326-339). No metric counts it, so nothing alerts. A blocked org also writes a new incident row on every daily sweep. The fix: (1) In internal/metrics/server.go, add an unlabelled-by-org counter audit_core_chain_purge_blocked_total with a single label "kind" (the bounded incident kinds in attest.go:41-49). Register it in init() and expose RecordChainPurgeBlocked(kind string). Keep the no-org-label rule stated in the comment at server.go:77-78. (2) In internal/store/attest.go blockPurge, call metrics.RecordChainPurgeBlocked(kind) after the incident insert succeeds. This fires in both dry-run and enabled modes, matching the incident row. (3) In apps/Control Plane/observability/rules/audit-core.rules.yml, add an alert ControlAuditChainPurgeBlocked: expr increase(audit_core_chain_purge_blocked_total[25h]) > 0, severity critical, plane control. The 25h window covers the daily sweep. Add a matching case to audit-core.rules.test.yml in the same style as the ControlAuditChainBroken cases. (4) Regression test: in internal/store/purge_chain_test.go, TestPurgeRefusesATamperedPrefixAndDeletesNothing (or a new test beside it) asserts that the counter for the incident kind rose by exactly 1 per blocked org. Reuse the counterValue helper pattern from chain_insert_test.go. Must NOT change: purge behaviour, incident rows, the switches (AUDIT_CHAIN_PRUNE_ENABLED and DRYRUN stay default off), and no org id, row content or details may go into any label. ZDR: the series is content-free. The files may be CRLF, so keep their line endings.
tests: go test ./internal/metrics/ ./internal/store/ -run 'Purge|DetailsGuard' -count=1  (the DB-backed purge tests need the audit-core Postgres test harness; they skip without it)

packets.title: audit-core verifier loop: a saved cursor above the chain head (after a restore) must reset, not report head_behind_chain
packets.brief: Defect: after audit tables are restored from an older copy, audit_chain_verifications.verified_through_seq can exceed the restored head. verifier.verifyOrg (internal/verifier/verifier.go:580-629) resumes from st.ThroughSeq (:593-594). Verify then reads no rows, so rangeEnd = FromSeq-1 > Head.Seq, and it returns broken/head_behind_chain (:380-381) with no real defect. Two things keep it there: the broken branch keeps the cursor (:605-609), and :620 only ever raises ThroughSeq, so every later pass repeats the false break. The fix, inside verifyOrg only: when the report is broken with ReasonHeadBehindChain and the run resumed from a stored cursor (opts.FromSeq > 0), log a warning (org id and the two sequence numbers only) and re-run once from the trust base (Options with FromSeq/FromHash zero and the same MaxRows). Use that report from then on. On a non-broken result, when the run started from the trust base and rep.Complete, set next.ThroughSeq/ThroughHash to rep's values even if they are lower than st.ThroughSeq, so the stale cursor is replaced. Keep the existing raise-only rule for incremental runs. A genuine head_behind_chain (rows beyond the head) must still end broken after the re-run, and verifyFailures must be incremented exactly once per pass. Regression tests go in internal/verifier/verifier_test.go using the existing fakeSource (around :600-720): the state has ThroughSeq above the fake head, a clean chain ends verified with ThroughSeq reset to the head and no failure counted, and a chain whose rows really extend past the head still ends broken with head_behind_chain and counts one failure. Must NOT change: the Verify() rules, the store package, the switches, or the broken-chain cursor behaviour for every other reason. The files may be CRLF, so keep their line endings.

packets.title: session-core: thread-aware SearchMemory/IndexMemory/learning announce, real org_learning_policy, Reset reaches Letta-only memories
packets.brief:
Service: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core (files are LF, keep LF). Four defects, all confirmed in the current tree.

(1) D1-573/D1-574 thread memory mode ignored by readers. memory_grpc.rs search_memory (call at ~line 383) and index_memory (calls at ~503 and ~524) use the user-level crate::memory_control::resolve(&self.pool,false,org,&owner_user_id). A thread whose threads.memory_mode='off' (WS07-S6) therefore still returns the user's rows from SearchMemory and still accepts IndexMemory. Change all three to crate::memory_control::resolve_for_thread(&self.pool,false,req.org_id.trim(),&owner_user_id,req.thread_id.trim()) (it already exists in memory_control.rs:409 and is a no-op when MEMORY_CONTROLS_ENABLED is falsey). Do NOT edit memory_control.rs or dreaming.rs (another packet owns them; the under-lock check inside dreaming::index_agent_memory is handled there).
   learning_events.rs enqueue_row (~line 330-344): inside the existing `if crate::memory_control::controls_enabled()` branch, after the user-level resolve, when identity.thread_id is Some, read the thread's mode on the same savepoint executor with `SELECT memory_mode FROM threads WHERE id = $1 AND org_id = $2` (fetch_optional) and fold it with the existing pub(crate) helpers: mode = value.map_or(ThreadMemoryMode::Inherit, |v| ThreadMemoryMode::from_wire(&v).unwrap_or(ThreadMemoryMode::Off)); decision = crate::memory_control::apply_thread_mode(decision, mode); if !decision.learning_allowed return Ok(Enqueued::SkippedMemoryState). Keep the lock-free read (no FOR UPDATE). The existing source-guard test around learning_events.rs:669 must keep passing.

(2) D1-597 GetMemoryControls reports org_learning_policy as "" (memory_grpc.rs:980). Add to org_policy.rs a pure fn `pub(crate) fn learning_policy_label(row: Option<&MirrorRow>, now: DateTime<Utc>, settings: &GateSettings) -> &'static str` returning: "" when !settings.governed (behaviour identical to today when the org policy is not configured); "unavailable" when view_from_row(...).memory == OrgMemoryPolicy::Unavailable; otherwise "proposals" if view_from_row(...).learning_review else "disabled". In memory_controls_view (memory_grpc.rs ~939): for a ZDR caller keep ""; else when controls_enabled() and settings().governed, read crate::org_policy::mirror_row(pool, org_id) and set org_learning_policy to the label; otherwise "". Do not change the proto (its comment already says the field is filled once the mirror exists).

(3) D1-552 ResetMemory leaves Letta-only memories. reset_memory (memory_grpc.rs ~865-920) erases only the semantic twins of durable ids returned by dreaming::reset_user_memory, but ListMemory (same file ~628-650) also shows Letta entries with no durable row, and those survive a 'Reset all memory'. After the durable reset and before erase_semantic_copies: when self.letta is Some, call letta.list_detailed(org_id, user_id, crate::memory_erasure::MAX_SEMANTIC_DELETES as u32); collect entries with a non-empty memory_id that are not already in `erased` (factor this into a pure helper, e.g. `fn semantic_only_ids(erased: &[String], listed: &[MemoryEntry]) -> Vec<String>`), insert them into forgotten_memory_ids (org_id, user_id, memory_id) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so recall stays suppressed even if a delete degrades, and append them to erased_rows (owner = user_id) so erase_semantic_copies deletes them. If the list itself is degraded (outcome.degradation_reason is Some), the response must report degraded=true with that reason (do not claim completeness). durable_deleted stays the durable count. Reset must remain user-only (service callers refused), confirm-required, and allowed for ZDR callers; no new content is written anywhere.

Tests to add (unit, no database): in org_policy.rs tests: learning_policy_label returns "" ungoverned, "unavailable" for fail-closed missing/stale row, "disabled" for memory_allowed=false or learning_mode='disabled', "proposals" for allowed+proposals. In memory_grpc.rs tests: semantic_only_ids excludes already-erased and empty ids and de-duplicates. Add a source-guard test in memory_grpc.rs asserting search_memory and index_memory bodies call memory_control::resolve_for_thread( and not memory_control::resolve( . Optionally an #[ignore] DATABASE_URL test that a thread set off gets empty SearchMemory with skip_reason thread_off and IndexMemory failed_precondition. Must NOT change: MEMORY_CONTROLS_ENABLED default-on semantics and its kill-switch behaviour, ORG_POLICY_* defaults, ZDR handling, delete paths staying ungated.

packets.title: session-core: per-thread resume watermark so messages written while a thread was off are never mined; IndexMemory under-lock thread check
packets.brief:
Service: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core (files are LF, keep LF). Defect: switching a thread's memory_mode from 'off' back to 'inherit' (UpdateThreadPresentation, grpc.rs ~7679-7721) moves no watermark. Dreaming's load_pending_messages and load_preceding_context (dreaming.rs ~1270-1360) only filter on user_memory_controls.extract_after, and memory_control::permits_extraction (memory_control.rs ~553-574) only checks the CURRENT memory_mode, so messages written while the thread was off are mined after it resumes. The user-level resume bumps extract_after; the thread toggle must behave the same.

Fix: (a) new migration migrations/0068_thread_memory_resumed_at.sql (next free session-core number per plan section 4.4; additive, idempotent): `ALTER TABLE threads ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS memory_resumed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL;` plus migrations/revert/0068_thread_memory_resumed_at.down.sql dropping it (follow 0067's style). (b) grpc.rs update_thread_presentation UPDATE: add `memory_resumed_at = CASE WHEN $13 AND memory_mode = 'off' AND $14 = 'inherit' THEN clock_timestamp() ELSE memory_resumed_at END` (SET expressions see the old row, so this fires only on an off->inherit transition); keep the existing lock_user call and event. (c) memory_control.rs permits_extraction SQL: add `AND (NOT $4 OR t.memory_resumed_at IS NULL OR m.created_at > t.memory_resumed_at)` ($4 is controls_enabled()). (d) dreaming.rs load_pending_messages and load_preceding_context: add the same conjunct gated on the controls_enabled bind they already have ($2 / $4 respectively), so the extractor neither reads nor is shown off-period turns. (e) Related D1-573 under-lock half: dreaming::index_agent_memory (~line 1646) calls memory_control::resolve_in_tx(&mut tx,false,org_id,owner_user_id); change to resolve_in_tx_for_thread(&mut tx,false,org_id,owner_user_id,thread_id) so a thread set off between the handler check and the write is refused under the lock; update the gates array in memory_control.rs every_agent_memory_writer_calls_the_gate (~line 1035-1039) from "resolve_in_tx(" to "resolve_in_tx_for_thread(" for that entry point. Do NOT edit memory_grpc.rs or learning_events.rs (another packet owns them).

Tests: unit/source-guard in memory_control.rs that permits_extraction's SQL contains memory_resumed_at; a test that the migration and its revert exist with the expected statements (pattern of org_policy.rs:590-595); an #[ignore = "requires DATABASE_URL to a disposable Postgres"] test in grpc.rs next to thread_off_blocks_read_and_write_for_that_thread_only (~line 4193): set a thread off, append a user message, set it back to inherit, append another, assert memory_resumed_at is set and permits_extraction is false for the first message and true for the second. Must NOT change: kill switch MEMORY_CONTROLS_ENABLED falsey restores old behaviour (all new conjuncts gated on it), inherit->off and inherit->inherit leave memory_resumed_at untouched, ZDR refusal of memory_mode unchanged, gateway still does not send memory_mode (http_routes.rs:9403 stays None). Also run the full session-core lib tests: this proves the WS07-S8 code (grpc.rs skill RPCs, gdpr.rs) now compiles and passes (D1-642).

packets.title: model-gateway: stage Ask-turn files into code_interpreter, type the vision_unsupported refusal, and filter the vision check by provider
packets.brief:
Three confirmed gaps in model-gateway's Ask (non-agentic) stream path, all in sse.rs.

(1) Files are accepted, then dropped. With CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED=true, attachment_policy.rs:174/264/296 accepts kind:"file" and declares modes.sandbox_files=true. But nothing calls turn_attachments::sandbox_staging_enabled() (turn_attachments.rs:32), and sse.rs:2913 calls tool_loop::run_tool_rounds_for_model. That wrapper (tool_loop.rs:6782-6812) always passes ValidatedAttachments::none(), so files validate and are silently ignored. Fix: in invoke_stream_sse, before any durable run is prepared (next to the image_parts/do_attachments admission at sse.rs:1543-1617, and only when the turn is not agentic), build `crate::turn_attachments::ValidatedAttachments::from_invoke(&req.attachments, crate::turn_attachments::sandbox_staging_enabled(), effective_zdr || retention_class.is_some())`. On Err(refusal), return error_stream(&request_id, refusal.code.as_str(), &refusal.message, false), the same as the Do path at sse.rs:1601-1611. Move the value into the spawned task. At sse.rs:2913, call crate::tool_loop::run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments(..., &staged, &image_parts) instead. Files must never be dropped silently: when staged is non-empty and the turn offers no code_interpreter tool (tool_defs empty, or no tool named code_interpreter), end the turn with a typed attachment refusal (AttachmentCode::MediaUnsupported, retryable false), not a silent drop. Put that check before the run is prepared if tool_defs is known there, otherwise as a prepared failure.

(2) vision_unsupported reads as an outage. inference-core refuses an image turn with FAILED_PRECONDITION plus the trailer x-mp-provider-error=vision_unsupported (inference-core grpc.rs:1700/1837). The gateway's direct-inference failure arm at sse.rs:7650-7671 only knows subscription failures and model_entitlement, so the refusal becomes code model_plane_unavailable with retryable:true, and terminal_code stays inference_unavailable (sse.rs:7611-7613). Fix: add a small helper in sse.rs that reads the trailer (crate::compaction::PROVIDER_ERROR_KIND_TRAILER) and recognises exactly "vision_unsupported". Use it to emit ChatEvent::Error { code: "vision_unsupported", message: a fixed sentence (the selected model cannot read images; pick a model that reads images or remove the image), retryable: false }, and use the same code as the terminal code. Do not change any other mapping.

(3) The vision check ignores the picked provider. The vision-capability check at sse.rs:1560-1566 sends ListModelsRequest::default(). Org model-access policy is already applied by inference-core (grpc.rs:518-525 filters chat models by the caller's principal), but the user's picked provider is not, so for a Verevon mode any listed vision model counts. Fix: set ListModelsRequest.provider to the turn's provider hint when one is non-empty (default otherwise). Check that the variable is in scope at that point; if it is not, derive it the same way the rest of the handler does.

Must NOT change: CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED, CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED and CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED stay default off; with the sandbox switch off, from_invoke returns none() and behaviour is byte-identical; a ZDR or waived turn never stages a file (refused); the Do-path admission is unchanged; no bytes or file names are logged (counts and sizes only, as turn_attachments.rs does); context_recovery_contract.rs must keep finding run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments. Do not edit attachment_policy.rs, vision_parts.rs or tool_loop.rs (other packets own them). Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Regression tests in sse.rs's test module:
(a) A pure helper test: switch on with a file attachment yields a non-empty ValidatedAttachments; switch off yields empty; ZDR or waived yields a refusal.
(b) The trailer helper maps a Status with x-mp-provider-error=vision_unsupported to code vision_unsupported, retryable false; another kind and a missing trailer map to None.
(c) The ListModelsRequest builder carries the provider hint when set and is the default when empty.

packets.title: execution-core: children get no attached files, RunInputs lives as long as the run, resumed runs refuse with attachments_expired
packets.brief:
Three confirmed defects in how execution-core holds a Do run's attached files (all behind CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED, which stays default off).

(1) Children inherit the parent's files. The code_interpreter arm of execute_step_inner reads `crate::run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id)` with no depth check (runtime_loop/mod.rs:893). A delegated child runs with the parent's run_id (agent.rs:5360, `req: parent.req`), so the child's code_interpreter stages the parent's attachments/. The plan says children do not inherit attachments, and the existing test children_do_not_inherit_attachments (agent.rs:26826) covers only images and the note. Fix: add a `read_run_inputs: bool` parameter to execute_step_with_result_handles and execute_step_inner (mod.rs:583/647). The agent loop call at agent.rs:3984 passes `ctx.depth == 0`. Every other caller (execute_step, execute_step_with_browser_grant, execute_step_with_subagent, and the test at mod.rs:2375) passes true, so their behaviour is identical. At mod.rs:893 write it as `let ro_inputs = if read_run_inputs { crate::run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id) } else { None };` so the literal `run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id)` that tests/cross_service_loop_contract.rs:463/545 pins is still present.

(2) The registry sweeps a live run's files. run_inputs.rs sweeps every entry older than DEFAULT_TTL (15 min, run_inputs.rs:32 and 267-278) on the next registration, even while the run's guard is alive, so a Do run longer than 15 minutes loses its files mid-run. Fix: store a per-entry expiry. Add `register_until(org_id, run_id, attachments, ttl: Duration)` and keep `register` as `register_until(.., self.ttl)`, so grpc.rs:1045 (ExecuteStep) is unchanged. The sweep compares against each entry's own expiry. register_run_inputs (agent.rs:2338, called at agent.rs:1609 inside the driver that has `deadline: RunDeadline`) passes the run deadline's remaining time from deadline.remaining_at(Instant::now()), never less than the default 15 min, and with a hard ceiling (for example 24 h) when the deadline has no limit, so a leaked guard is still evicted.

(3) A resumed run is told about files it no longer has. A parked, in-place-resumed or continuation Do run loses its files, because the guard lives only inside run_agent. The restored or parked messages (agent.rs:2531-2545) still hold the sandbox note that says attachments/ exists. The plan (build plan WS08-S6 row) says a resumed Do run re-requests attachments, with refusal reason `attachments_expired`, rather than persisting them. Fix:
- In mp-contracts attachments.rs, add `pub const ATTACHMENTS_EXPIRED: &str = "attachments_expired";` and `pub fn is_sandbox_note(content: &str) -> bool`, which matches the fixed first sentence that sandbox_note writes.
- In run_rounds, on the restored and parked branches, when any restored message is a system message for which is_sandbox_note is true and the request carries no file attachments (split_attachments(&req.attachments).0 is empty), return Err(tonic::Status::failed_precondition(ATTACHMENTS_EXPIRED)) before the first inference round. Do this before any tool runs.
- Check that this refusal does not consume a granted approval a second time and leaves the run as the other resume refusals do. If the refusal can only be raised after the approval is consumed, raise it there and record that in a comment.

Must NOT change: the switch stays default off; a run without attachments behaves byte-identically (no note, nothing registered, no refusal); ZDR runs never carry files; no bytes or names are logged; register's public behaviour for ExecuteStep is unchanged. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Tests to add:
(a) In agent.rs: a child that calls code_interpreter sees no ro_inputs (extend children_do_not_inherit_attachments, or add a_child_code_interpreter_step_sees_no_attached_files, asserting the registry lookup is skipped at depth 1).
(b) In run_inputs.rs: an entry registered with a long TTL survives a sweep_at(now + 16 min), and a default entry does not.
(c) In agent.rs: an in-place or parked resume whose restored messages hold the sandbox note, with no attachments on the request, fails with attachments_expired; the same resume without the note proceeds.
(d) In mp-contracts: is_sandbox_note is true for sandbox_note output and false for arbitrary text.

packets.title: execution-core code_interpreter: do not chmod through a planted attachments symlink in a persistent Space root
packets.brief:
code_interpreter.rs stages attached files into <root>/attachments. StagedInputs::stage (code_interpreter.rs:686-725) first calls remove_staged_dir(root/attachments) (line 706). remove_staged_dir (lines 736-745) calls set_mode(dir, 0o755), which is std::fs::set_permissions and follows symlinks, then remove_dir_all. In a persistent Space root (run_in_root with persistent=true, line 577; reached from the Do-attachments path), a program from an earlier call of the same run can plant `attachments` as a symlink to a host path. The next staging call then chmods the target as the execution-core user.

Fix remove_staged_dir: first read std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir).
- NotFound: return quietly.
- A symlink or any non-directory: std::fs::remove_file it, with no chmod.
- A real directory: chmod and remove as today.
Also make Drop for StagedInputs and the create_dir path safe: create_dir must fail rather than follow a symlink that reappears (it already does on unix, since create_dir does not follow a final symlink; keep it so). Do not change the reserved-name rule (files_in may not be named attachments, line 288).

Must NOT change: the ephemeral path; read-only modes 0o444/0o555; staging is still refused where the OS sandbox is unavailable; nothing logs file content. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Tests to add, in code_interpreter.rs tests and #[cfg(unix)] because they need symlinks and modes:
(a) remove_staged_dir on a symlink `attachments` that points to a directory with mode 0o500: the link is removed and the target's mode is unchanged.
(b) remove_staged_dir on a regular file named attachments removes it.
(c) remove_staged_dir on a staged read-only directory removes it.
(d) A persistent-root test (D1-608): two successive stagings into the same root both succeed, the second after a leftover attachments directory.
Note for the tester: these tests compile to nothing on Windows; run them on Linux (the rust:1 Docker recipe) or record them as unix-only.

packets.title: DashboardComposer registers a stale-build reload guard for unsent attachments
packets.brief:
WS09-S5 chunk recovery (src/app/chunk-recovery.ts) reloads the page once when a lazy chunk 404s after a deploy. It is on by default: only VITE_CHUNK_RECOVERY_DISABLED=true turns it off. Features that hold state only in memory must call registerReloadGuard(isDirty) (chunk-recovery.ts:42) so the reload is replaced by a notice. Only use-chat-controller.ts:455 registers one, and it covers only streaming and input text. DashboardComposer.tsx holds unsent attached files in its own `files` signal (line 1010) and registers no guard, so a stale-build reload silently discards attachments that have not been sent, on both Home and Chat.

Fix: in DashboardComposer, import registerReloadGuard from '@/app/chunk-recovery' and call `onCleanup(registerReloadGuard(() => files().length > 0))` in the component body (onCleanup is already imported, line 65). Optionally include an in-flight handoff (handoffPending()).

Must NOT change: the composer's behaviour otherwise; chunk-recovery.ts itself; the existing controller guard. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Test: add DashboardComposer.reload-guard.test.tsx. Render the composer, add a file through the existing paste or attach test path (see DashboardComposer.paste-attachment.test.tsx), and assert that a vite:preloadError dispatch does not reload but shows staleBuildNotice; with no files it does reload. Mock window.location.reload as chunk-recovery.test.ts does.

packets.title: inference-core: effort ceilings also bound the legacy thinking budget, and the org policy max_effort is applied at the PEP (covers the agentic path)
packets.brief:
Two effort ceilings in inference-core leave holes.

(1) Budget clamp, legacy budget (D1-032/033). In `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/fallback.rs`, `resolve_intent` (around lines 1079-1098) clamps only `rewritten.reasoning_effort` (an `Option<effort::Level>`) to `decision.effort_cap` when `effort::budget_clamp_enabled()` (env `INFERENCE_CORE_EFFORT_BUDGET_CLAMP`, only the literal `true`). The first half of the row (reasoning_effort never reaching InferRequest) is fixed: model-gateway now sets it (`thinking.rs`, `sse.rs:3068`, `http_routes.rs:10519`) and `grpc.rs:1230` maps it. What is still wrong: when `reasoning_effort` is `None` (gateway ladder switch `MODEL_GATEWAY_EFFORT_LADDER` off), the request carries the legacy `thinking_budget_tokens` and that is never clamped, so an exhausted-budget org still spends the full legacy budget. Fix: when the clamp is on and `decision.effort_cap` is `Some(cap)` and `reasoning_effort` is `None` and `thinking_budget_tokens > 0`, set `thinking_budget_tokens = min(thinking_budget_tokens, effort::allowance(cap))` and log it with the same content-free `clamped = true` info line. Put the arithmetic in a small pure helper in `provider/effort.rs` (e.g. `pub fn cap_legacy_budget(budget: i32, cap: Option<Level>) -> i32`: never raises, `None` cap and `budget <= 0` return the input unchanged) so it is unit-testable.

(2) Org policy max_effort is not applied at the PEP (D1-499). Only model-gateway clamps the effort to the policy's `max_effort` (`model_access.rs` `Admitted::clamp_effort`, called from `sse.rs:1197` and `http_routes.rs:10474`). execution-core's agent loop calls inference-core directly (RunAgentRequest path), so a role capped at e.g. `low` can still run a deep agent loop. inference-core is the enforcement point and already carries the caller's entitlement on `InferRequest.access` (`Option<Arc<RequestAccess>>`, set by `with_access` in grpc.rs). Fix in fallback.rs: add one helper applied in BOTH `infer_with_response_cache` (after `pinned_model`/`resolve_intent`, line ~1303-1309) and `infer_stream` (line ~1721-1723), BEFORE the response-cache lookup (the cache key hashes the effort level): when `req.access` is `Some(access)` and `access.enforced()` and the resolved policy has a non-empty `max_effort` (use `access.resolved().clamp_effort(name)` from `mp_contracts::model_entitlement::ResolvedAccess`, or `Level::from_name` + `effort::clamp_to_cap`), lower `reasoning_effort` to the ceiling, and when `reasoning_effort` is `None` cap `thinking_budget_tokens` with the same `cap_legacy_budget` helper. Clamp down only, never up; an unknown ceiling name leaves the request alone (it is validated at write time by org-core). Since `req` is `&InferRequest`, clone only when a change is needed.

Must NOT change: with `INFERENCE_CORE_EFFORT_BUDGET_CLAMP` unset and `MODEL_ENTITLEMENT_MODE` off/shadow the request is byte-identical to today (no clamp, no clone visible in behaviour); a service principal (access None / exempt) is never clamped; no content in logs (ids, level names, numbers only). Keep the files' existing line endings (check CRLF vs LF before editing).

Regression tests (unit, in the files' existing `#[cfg(test)]` modules): effort.rs `cap_legacy_budget` cases (4096 capped to 1024 by Low, 512 under Low unchanged, 0 and negative unchanged, None cap unchanged); fallback.rs: a request with `access` enforced and a policy max_effort `low` and `reasoning_effort = Some(High)` reaches the provider (use the existing mock provider pattern in fallback.rs tests, e.g. the tests near `preserves_explicitly_pinned_model` / `the_streaming_path_honors_a_pinned_model`) with `Low`; the same with `reasoning_effort = None, thinking_budget_tokens = 4096` reaches it with 1024; the same request under shadow (not enforced) reaches it unchanged; one streaming-path case.
tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p inference-core --lib provider::effort
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p inference-core --lib provider::fallback

packets.title: org-core refuses verevon-* intent ids in allow/deny lists
packets.brief: A model policy entry naming a Verevon intent id (`verevon-budget`, `verevon-balance`, `verevon-genius`, any `verevon-*`) is never matched by inference-core: intent ids pass the entitlement check as an unspecified model and an Auto request is judged only on the concrete model the intent layer resolves (`inference-core/src/provider/fallback.rs` `pinned_model`/`resolve_intent`). So an admin who denies `verevon-genius` believes they blocked it and nothing happens. org-core's validator (`apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/modelentitlement/validate.go`, `normalizeEntry` lines 210-234, used by `entries` for both `allow` and `deny`) accepts such entries today. Fix: in `entries` (allow and deny only), refuse an entry whose normalised form starts with `verevon-` with a new stable code `CodeIntentIDNotAllowed = "intent_id_not_allowed"` (add it to the const block at lines 22-42) and a message saying intent modes are not models and the policy judges the concrete model they resolve to. Do NOT refuse it as a surface default model (`defaults` path, a default of an intent id is a legitimate Auto default) and do not touch `provider:` selectors. Add table cases to `validate_test.go`: `verevon-genius` in allow (listed) and in deny refused with that code at the right JSON path (`org_default.deny[0]`, `roles.x.allow[1]`), `VEREVON-Budget ` (case/space folded) refused, a model id that merely contains `verevon` later in the string accepted, and a defaults model `verevon-balance` still accepted. If `testdata/model-entitlement-matrix.json` is a shared golden pinned elsewhere, do not edit it. Keep the file's existing line endings. The Auto/no_entitled_route part of D1-477 is accepted by the plan row and needs a live proof, not code.

packets.title: Prometheus: ZDR attestation review-due / lapsed alerts, promtool tests, inference-core :8082 scrape
packets.brief:
inference-core publishes gauge `mp_inference_zdr_attestation_review_by_timestamp_seconds{surface=...}` (rust/services/inference-core/src/metrics.rs:53-58, 247-257): Unix seconds at the START of the review-by UTC day; the attestation stops granting ZDR after that day; absent for a surface with no ZDR claim. No alert rule reads it and Prometheus does not scrape inference-core, so a lapse is visible only in logs.

Do: (1) Add scrape job `model-inference-core` to apps/Control Plane/observability/prometheus.yml, metrics_path /metrics, target `model-plane-inference-core-1:8082` (the plane-unique inter-plane-bus alias declared in apps/Model Plane/deploy/docker-compose.yml:1146-1151; the bare `inference-core` alias also exists but follow the existing model-* pattern), labels { service: inference-core, plane: model }, placed next to the model-session-core/model-gateway jobs with a one-line comment. (2) New rules file apps/Control Plane/observability/rules/zdr-attestation.rules.yml (picked up by the existing `rule_files: /etc/prometheus/rules/*.rules.yml`), group `model-zdr-attestation`, in the style of audit-delivery.rules.yml: ZdrAttestationReviewDue warning when `min by (surface) (mp_inference_zdr_attestation_review_by_timestamp_seconds) - time() < 14*86400`, critical when `< 3*86400` (two rules or two severities - make the critical one not double-fire the warning wording; keep label plane: model and a runbook annotation); ZdrAttestationLapsed critical when `time() - min by (surface) (mp_inference_zdr_attestation_review_by_timestamp_seconds) > 86400`. Header comment: why, no pager yet (decision D1), series are content-free. (3) New promtool test file rules/zdr-attestation.rules.test.yml with firing and quiet cases: far-future review-by stays quiet; 10 days out fires warning only; 2 days out fires critical; review-by 2 days in the past fires Lapsed; no series = no alerts. Use `eval_time` and constant series values computed from the test's time origin (promtool time starts at 0, so time() at eval_time 10m is 600). (4) Add a short `## Attestation lapse alerts` section with an anchor to apps/Model Plane/docs/runbooks/zdr-attestation-and-live-proof.md naming the three alerts and what to do (renew the attestation, re-sign the policy), and point the runbook annotations there.

Must not change: existing jobs and rules; no Alertmanager wiring. prometheus.yml is CRLF in this worktree (attr eol=lf) - preserve the existing line endings; new rule files LF like their siblings.

packets.title: cross-plane preflight: fail closed when rg is missing or errors
packets.brief: scripts/coresystem-cross-plane-preflight.sh check_evidence_open (lines 156-167) runs `rg -q -- "$pattern" "$MODEL_EVIDENCE"` in an elif; when rg is not installed (exit 127) or errors (exit 2) the else branch prints `state=recorded` and adds no blocker, so a missing tool reads as release evidence recorded (fail open). Fix: (1) right after argument parsing and BEFORE the docker check (line ~31), add `command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "BLOCKED rg: command is unavailable"; exit 2; }` mirroring the docker check; (2) in check_evidence_open capture rg's status explicitly (the script runs set -euo pipefail, so use `set +e`/`rc=$?` or `if rg ...; then ... else rc=$?` pattern): 0 -> state=open + `${label}_evidence_open`; 1 -> state=recorded; anything else -> state=unreadable + blocker `${label}_evidence_unreadable`. Regression test in scripts/tests/coresystem-cross-plane-preflight-test.sh, placed BEFORE the existing live-stack section: build a temp bin dir containing only a symlink/copy of `dirname` (the only external the script needs before the new rg check), run `PATH="$tmpbin" "$BASH" "$COMMAND"` and assert exit 2 and output contains `BLOCKED rg`; clean up with trap. Must not change: any other check, exit codes 0/2/64, read-only/no-secret behaviour. Files are LF (attr eol=lf). Note the rest of the test needs a running stack; the coder proves the new case alone (it runs first and exits on failure) and reports the live part as not run.

packets.title: conformance gate: tie a PASSED rollback rehearsal to the candidate and rollback artifacts under review
packets.brief: rollback-rehearsal.sh already records both digests in the evidence file (apps/Model Plane/scripts/rollback-rehearsal.sh:288-289: lines `candidate: revision <rev>, root manifest sha256 <hex>` and `rollback: revision <rev>, root manifest sha256 <hex>`), but scripts/coresystem-conformance.sh (rehearsal block lines ~185-216) only checks `result PASSED` on line 1 and the file date, so a rehearsal of any other artifacts passes the gate. Fix in coresystem-conformance.sh: when MODEL_PLANE_CANDIDATE_ARTIFACT_DIR and MODEL_PLANE_ROLLBACK_ARTIFACT_DIR are both set and the rehearsal state would be `passed`, compute sha256 of "$candidate_dir/artifact-manifest.tsv" and "$rollback_dir/artifact-manifest.tsv" (sha256sum, fall back to `shasum -a 256` if absent; strip CR when reading the evidence file) and require the evidence file's candidate and rollback lines to name exactly those digests; otherwise set rehearsal_state=mismatch and add blocker `rollback_rehearsal_artifact_mismatch` (an empty/missing digest line is a mismatch). Add `rollback_rehearsal_artifact_mismatch` to the unwaivable set in the embedded python (`unwaivable()`, ~line 335) because a rehearsal of other artifacts is not evidence. When either artifact dir is unset keep today's behaviour (the artifact_missing blockers already block). Update the --help text's runtime profile line to say the rehearsal must match the artifacts. Tests in scripts/tests/coresystem-conformance-artifact-test.sh, next to the existing rehearsal cases (~lines 172-185): create good-candidate/good-rollback artifact-manifest.tsv fixtures (if not already present), write a PASSED evidence file with matching digest lines and assert checks.rollback_rehearsal == passed with artifact dirs set; a file with a wrong candidate digest -> `rollback_rehearsal_artifact_mismatch` in blockers and not waivable by a waiver row; a PASSED file without digest lines and artifact dirs set -> mismatch; the existing no-artifact rehearsal cases keep their current expectations. Must not change: rollback-rehearsal.sh output format, other blockers, JSON shape apart from the new state/blocker value. Files are LF (attr eol=lf).

packets.title: CAPABILITY_PROMOTION_LEDGER.tsv: add the capability IDs seeded by capability-core migrations
packets.brief: apps/Model Plane/scripts/tests/capability-promotion-ledger-test.sh requires the ledger IDs to equal exactly the `'cap.*` IDs seeded in go/services/capability-core/migrations/*.sql; conformance (scripts/coresystem-conformance.sh:218-235) reports capability_promotion_ledger_invalid when it fails. A diff today shows SIX IDs missing from apps/Model Plane/docs/CAPABILITY_PROMOTION_LEDGER.tsv (the row named five; cap.result.query has since been added by migration 0013): cap.agent.lineage.read, cap.memory.index, cap.memory.search, cap.process.background, cap.result.query, cap.skill.summarize. Add one row each with state source_only and the source_only shape the test enforces: `<id>\tsource_only\tworking-tree\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tNo immutable candidate or live owner evidence.` (9 tab-separated columns), keeping the file's existing ordering convention. Must not change: any existing row's state, the cap.tool.ticket.create source_only rule, the header. Preserve the ledger's existing line endings (CRLF in the worktree).

packets.title: model-gateway: renew the shared Pending idempotency claim while the owning stream runs
packets.brief:
With MODEL_GATEWAY_SHARED_IDEMPOTENCY on (WS04-S7), `CommitGuard::claim_shared` (src/idempotency_registry.rs about 431) takes a Redis `SET NX PX` claim for PENDING_TTL = 120 s (about line 68 and 554) and nothing renews it. A stream that runs longer than 120 s lets a duplicate send on another replica win a fresh claim and start a second run.

Fix: add `fn renew<'a>(&'a self, key: &'a str, request_id: &'a str) -> BoxFuture<'a, bool>` to the `SharedClaimStore` trait: extend the key's TTL to PENDING_TTL only while the stored value is still this request's Pending claim (same read-then-write pattern as `settle`, using `PEXPIRE key ttl_ms`; return false if the key is gone or belongs to another request). Implement it for RedisClaimStore and for the test fake `FakeShared` (about line 879). In claim_shared's `Won` branch spawn a renewal task (tokio, only when a runtime is present) that every PENDING_TTL/3 calls renew and stops when renew returns false; keep its `JoinHandle`/abort handle in `SharedRelease` and abort it in `CommitGuard::drop` before spawning `settle`, so a Done or deleted claim is never re-extended. A renewal failure is logged by operation only (never the key: it holds org and user ids) through the existing `run` breaker.

Tests (idempotency_registry.rs test module, with the fake and tokio time pause): the claim's fake TTL is extended while the guard lives; after the guard drops no further renew is issued and settle runs; renew does nothing for a key now owned by another request_id.

Must NOT change: switch default off and the local registry's behaviour (PENDING_TTL for the local map stays as is); `SharedClaimValue` shape (ids and state only, never answer text); DONE_TTL semantics. Preserve CRLF.
tests: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/dev/mp-target-w2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -q -p model-gateway --lib idempotency_registry

packets.title: Infra core-gateway: remove the default Postgres DSN that embeds a literal password
packets.brief:
apps/Infra Plane/core-gateway/internal/config/config.go line ~233 sets `viper.SetDefault("database.postgresurl", "postgres://coresystem:<literal password>@postgres:5432/coresystem?sslmode=disable")`. It names the legacy coresystem database and puts a credential in source; it applies whenever DATABASE_POSTGRESURL is unset (configs/config.yaml already says postgres_url is set via that env var). Do not print or copy the password anywhere (commit message, test, log).

Fix: delete that SetDefault line (no default DSN). Then make the only consumer safe with an empty URL: internal/health/checker.go `CheckPostgreSQL` (about line 55) must not call sql.Open with an empty DSN (lib/pq would then dial localhost from PG* env); when `d.postgresURL` is empty return a PostgreSQLHealth with Status "not_configured" and no error string, without opening a connection. Check cmd/gateway/main.go (about line 111) still compiles unchanged.

Tests: new internal/config/config_test.go asserting that after setDefaults() `viper.GetString("database.postgresurl")` is empty and that the file contains no `postgres://` literal with userinfo (read config.go and assert no match for `postgres(ql)?://[^/@\s]+:[^/@\s]+@`); new internal/health/checker_test.go asserting CheckPostgreSQL with an empty URL returns "not_configured" quickly. Note for the lead (not code): the removed password must be treated as exposed and rotated wherever that legacy database still runs.

Must NOT change: other defaults, validate() rules, any other service. Preserve line endings.

packets.title: plane-boundary gate: --base-ref fails a change that relaxes the allowlist
packets.brief:
scripts/gates/plane-boundary.py reads scripts/gates/plane-boundary.json (keys local_hosts, planes[*].db_hosts, shared_hosts, db_exceptions, manifest_exceptions) and has no base comparison, so the same change that adds a cross-plane reference can add the exception that hides it. scripts/gates/size-ratchet.py already has the pattern to copy (`--base-ref`, `compare_with_base`, git show of the base file, fail closed when the ref does not resolve, skip with a note when the base has no config file).

Do: add `--base-ref REF` to plane-boundary.py's --check. Load the policy at the base with `git show REF:scripts/gates/plane-boundary.json` (through the existing Policy validator) and report a problem for every relaxation: a new (file, host) in db_exceptions or (file, target) in manifest_exceptions; a host added to any plane's db_hosts; a new shared_hosts key; a new local_hosts entry; a plane newly listed. Removals and reason-text edits are not relaxations. Also detect a change to the rule constants a change could loosen (SOURCE_SUFFIXES dropping a suffix, TEST_DIRS gaining an entry, CROSS_DB_LINKS losing a pattern) by reading them from the base script with ast, as size-ratchet's policy_at does. Exit codes unchanged (1 problems, 2 cannot run).

Wire it in .github/workflows/repo-gates.yml plane-boundary job exactly like the size-ratchet job: checkout with fetch-depth 0, and a bash step that passes --base-ref "origin/$BASE_REF" on pull_request, "$BEFORE_SHA" on push when it resolves, else plain --check. Keep `continue-on-error: true` (rollout convention).

Tests in scripts/tests/test_plane_boundary.py using a throwaway git repo (copy the Repo helper approach from scripts/tests/test_size_ratchet.py): a change adding a db_exception fails against the base; adding a host to a plane fails; removing an exception passes; an unknown base ref exits 2; a base without the config file is not compared. Keep `--self-test` fixtures passing.

Out of scope (owner decision, DEC-39 D2): a CODEOWNERS entry; the repository has no CODEOWNERS file today. Must NOT change: the R1-R3 rules or their output for --check without --base-ref.

packets.title: size-ratchet: a baselined file renamed out of the count fails against the base
packets.brief:
scripts/gates/size-ratchet.py `relaxations`/`compare_with_base` (about lines 170-200) compares ceilings by path. A file that has a ceiling at the base and is `git mv`-ed into a `gen/` directory, under `target`/`dist`/`node_modules`, or to an uncounted suffix simply disappears from the count; --update drops its entry and the base comparison sees no raise, so the file escapes the ratchet. The docstring admits it ("A rename that moves a file out of the count is not detected").

Fix: in compare_with_base, for each path in the BASE baseline that is no longer a counted file now (`counts.get(path) is None`), ask git for renames between the base and the tree being checked: `git diff --name-status -z -M <base_ref>` against the working tree (or `<base_ref> <ref>` when --ref is given). If the path was renamed (R status) to a destination that is not counted (not in counts, or counts[dest] is None as generated), report `<old>: renamed to <new>, which is not counted; a baselined file cannot leave the count by moving`. A destination that IS counted is handled by the existing rules (it is over the cap with no ceiling unless the baseline moves with it — and a new entry for it must not exceed the old ceiling: treat a renamed entry's allowance as the old path's ceiling in the raise check). A plain deletion (D) stays allowed. Update the module docstring sentence accordingly.

Tests in scripts/tests/test_size_ratchet.py (use the existing Repo helper): a baselined file git-mv'ed into gen/ fails with --base-ref; renamed to an uncounted suffix fails; renamed to another counted path with its ceiling carried over passes; deleted outright passes.

Must NOT change: CAP, counted suffixes, --update/--init behaviour, exit codes.

packets.title: verevonv3: keep vitest from collecting the node:test bundle-budget test
packets.brief:
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/scripts/check-bundle-budget.test.mjs (WS12-S12) is a node:test file run by CI with `node --test` (.github/workflows/verevonv3-ci.yml about line 198). vite.config.ts test.exclude (about lines 83-104) excludes 'apps/gateway/scripts/**/*.test.mjs' but not 'scripts/**/*.test.mjs', and vitest's default include matches .test.mjs, so `pnpm test` (vitest run) collects it and fails. Fix: add `'scripts/**/*.test.mjs',` to test.exclude with a one-line comment (node:test file, run by `node --test` in CI). Nothing else changes.

Proof: `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/check-bundle-budget.test.mjs --passWithNoTests` reports no test files collected (before the fix it collects and fails), and `node --test scripts/check-bundle-budget.test.mjs` still passes. Preserve line endings.
